title: The red fox at dusk
body: The red fox is a master of twilight hunting. With sharp hearing and pouncing leaps, a red fox can catch mice under deep snow. Its bushy tail balances each jump.

title: Vulpes vulpes, up close
body: Vulpes vulpes is the largest species of the genus Vulpes. Found across the Northern Hemisphere, this wild fox species adapts from forests to farmland.

title: Foxes in the city
body: Urban foxes roam our suburbs at night. A wild red fox learns traffic patterns, raids bins, and raises cubs in quiet gardens.

title: Gray wolf packs
body: The gray wolf, Canis lupus, lives in family packs led by an alpha pair. Howling binds the pack across miles of wilderness.

title: Wolves of Yellowstone
body: When wolves returned to Yellowstone, elk behavior changed, riverside willows recovered, and the whole ecosystem shifted. The grey wolf is a keystone predator.

title: Wolf or dog?
body: Wolves and dogs share an ancestor, but a wild wolf hunts cooperatively and avoids human contact. A wolf's paws are larger than a dog's.

title: Man's best friend
body: The domestic dog has lived beside humans for thousands of years. From herding to companionship, dogs read human gestures better than any other animal.

title: Puppy development
body: A puppy opens its eyes around two weeks old. Early socialization shapes a calm adult dog, and play builds coordination.

title: Working dogs
body: Border collies herd sheep, labradors retrieve, and huskies pull sleds. Working dog breeds thrive with a job to do.

title: Bears and hibernation
body: In winter, a bear settles into its den. Heart rate drops, and the mother bear gives birth while sleeping through the cold months.

title: The brown bear's diet
body: A brown bear eats berries, roots, salmon, and insects. Before winter, an adult bear may gain thousands of calories a day.

title: Bears in folklore
body: From forest spirits to storybook characters, the bear looms large in human folklore, and bear cubs playing in the woods remain a beloved image.

title: Deer and their antlers
body: Male deer grow antlers each spring and shed them in winter. During the rut, stags clash in the forest.

title: Graceful deer of the forest
body: A deer freezes at the sound of a twig. Its ears swivel toward every rustle before it bounds away.

title: Cervidae around the world
body: The family Cervidae spans red deer, elk, and tiny muntjacs. Deer inhabit forests, grasslands, and mountains.
